claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, his eligibility depends on what he's currently doing. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me, is Alex currently in full-time education, training, or has he left education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education at the moment. He finished school recently and hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Since Alex is 16 and has recently left education, there's a possibility you could still receive Child Benefit for him for a limited period.

Has Alex registered with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England), or
- The armed services?

If a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with one of these, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with the careers service or the armed forces. He's just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you, or do you contribute financially towards his care (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK, and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just one more question to complete my assessment:

Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more a week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started working, and he's not receiving any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK
- Alex is 16 years old and lives with you
- Alex has left education and is not in approved education or training
- Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- Alex is not working 24+ hours a week and is not receiving benefits in his own right

Unfortunately, since Alex is 16 and has left education without registering with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you would not currently be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

**However**, if Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service) or the armed services, you could apply for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks. Alternatively, if Alex returns to approved education or training, you could continue to receive Child Benefit until he turns 20.

Let me provide my formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Summary

**Alex (age 16):** ❌ Not eligible

Since Alex is 16 and has left education, Child Benefit would normally only continue if he:
- Stays in approved education or training (until age 20), OR
- Registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (for up to 20 weeks)

Since neither of these currently applies, you wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

### What you could do next

If Alex is considering his options, encouraging him to register with a government-sponsored careers service could allow you to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks while he decides on his next steps. Alternatively, if he returns to approved education or training, you would be able to claim Child Benefit again.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?
